data.text:
Chukkala Vineel Kumar And 3 Others vs The Telangana State
Public Service ... on 12 February, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.45153 Of 2022
O R D E R: 
This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking the following relief:
"...to issue any appropriate writ, order or direction one particularly one in the nature writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondents, in treating the Women Reservation also as the Vertical Reservation, instead of treating it as the Horizontal Reservation, in the Notification No.06/2022, Dated 21/07/2022, for the notified Food Safety Officer Posts, issued by the 1st respondent, under the guise of implementing the 33.33% reservation in favour of women candidates, in terms of Rule 22 & 22-A of Telangana State and Subordinate Service Rules, 1996, as arbitrary,
illegal and violative of Articles 14, 16 and 21 of the Constitution of India and contrary to the Dicta laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajesh Kumar Dania Vs. Rajastan Public Service Commission and others reported in AIR 2007 SC 3127 and Public Service Commission, Uttaranchal Vs. Mamta Bisht and others reported in 2010 (12) SCC 204, and in the case of K.Venkatesh and Another Vs.
Government of AP and others reported in 2009 (6) ALT 483 and consequently read down the Notification No.06/2022, dated 21.07.2022, issued by the 1st respondent,
in so far as Women Reservation is concerned, set-aside the 100 point roster prescribed in Rules 22 and 22-A of Telangana State & Subordinate Service Rules,
1996, in so far as women roster points are concerned, and direct the respondents to follow the principles of Horizontal Reservation for Women Candidates in the 33.33%
reservation in favour of women, without earmarking any roster points for them and by following the procedure indicated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases reported in AIR 2007 SC 3127 and 2010 (12) SCC 204, by counting the meritorious women candidates also against the number of special reservation quota for women and accordingly consider the cases of the petitioners and other aspirants for appointment as Food Safety Officers, based on their merit, against the notified Food Safety Officer Posts, pursuant to the Notification No.06/2022, dated 21.07.2022 issued by the 1st respondent and pass..." 
2. Heard Sri J.Sudheer, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners; Sri M.Ramgopal Rao, learned Standing Counsel for TSPSC appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 and learned Government Pleader for Services - III appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3.

1 3. When the matter came up for admission on 19.12.2022, this Court granted an interim order,
which reads as under:
"Notice before admission. 
The learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajesh Kumar Daria Vs. Rajasthan public service Commission and others [AIR 2007 SCC 3127]. In the said Judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court directed to follow the principles of Horizontal Reservation for Women Candidates without earmarking any roster points for them. 
Learned Government Pleader seeks time to file counter. 
However, since there is a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is settled law, the respondents are, therefore, directed to follow the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raiesh Kumar Daria Vs. Rajasthan Public Service Commission and others in [AIR 2007 SCC 3127] while making appointments to the post of Food Safety Officers."
List the matter after four (04) weeks."
4. Today, when the matter is taken up for hearing, learned Government Pleader for Services-III appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3, on production of a copy of the Memo No.4981/Ser.D/A2/2023, issued by respondent No.2, submits that respondent No.2 has directed respondent No.1 to comply with the aforesaid interim order of this Court, dated 19.12.2022. 
Therefore, learned counsel prayed this Court to dispose the matter. 
5. In view of the above, the interim order, dated 19.12.2022 is hereby made absolute and the respondents are directed to go ahead with the selections as per the interim order, dated 19.12.2022.
6. With the above observation, this Writ Petition is disposed of. There shall be no order as to costs. 
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed. 
______________________ PULLA KARTHIK, J Date : 12.02.2024 TMK Chukkala Vineel Kumar And 3 Others vs The Telangana State Public Service ... on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195241741/
